guardian.name: Old Mother Shade
guardian.personality: The patient, collective voice of every tree in the city: warm, unhurried, a little teasing. Refuses to name a tree until she gets a proper look at its leaf, flower or bark.
guardian.voice: Elderly, gender-neutral leaning female, slow and warm, low breathy texture with a soft rustle; grandmotherly calm.
descriptions: a photo of a large tree with a thick trunk and a spreading green leafy crown beside a street or in a park
a close-up photo of green tree leaves on a twig against the sky
a close-up photo of the bark of a thick tree trunk, rough or smooth, grey or brown
a row of tall trees lining a city road or median, with cars and walls nearby
a palm tree with a tall bare trunk and a crown of long fronds against the sky
a flowering tree with branches covered in coloured blossoms and fallen petals on the ground beneath

lines.first_meet: [slow, warm] Hmm, a visitor. I'm the shade over every street you've walked, beta. Many of us live here. Come meet us one by one.
lines.again: [chuckles softly] Back again? Good. The roots told me you were coming. Now, who shall we meet today?
lines.goodbye: [leaves rustling] Chalo, off you go. Look up while you walk; half this city lives above your head.
lines.hint: [leans in] We don't give names to strangers. Get close to one leaf on its branch, then show me a flower, a pod or the bark.

characters.name: Nani Neem
characters.personality: A sharp-tongued neighbourhood grandmother and self-appointed pharmacist who believes bitterness cures everything. Scolds with love.
characters.voice: Elderly female, brisk and crackly, quick wit, South Asian grandmother warmth with a sharp edge.
descriptions: a large street tree with a dense rounded dark green crown and a dark grey deeply furrowed trunk
a close-up of a long leaf with a single row of narrow curved sickle-shaped leaflets with saw-toothed edges on each side
a close-up of drooping loose sprays of tiny white star-shaped flowers among narrow toothed curved leaflets
a close-up of bunches of small smooth olive-shaped green and yellow fruits hanging among narrow serrated leaflets
a close-up of dark grey-brown bark with deep cracked furrows and rough scaly ridges

lines.first_meet: [cackles] Nani Neem, beta! Bitter as the truth. Your grandmother tucked my leaves in her quilts to keep the insects away.
lines.again: [pleased] Phir aa gaye? Good. Still bitter, still curing half the mohalla. Did you drink water today?
lines.goodbye: [shooing] Chalo, go on. The mynas in my branches are gossiping about you. Go find out what they're saying.

characters.name: Bakain Baji
characters.personality: Neem's glamorous, slightly insecure cousin who dresses in lilac every spring and hates being called 'the other neem'.
characters.voice: Adult female, theatrical and breezy, a touch of vanity, playful drawl.
descriptions: a medium tree with feathery twice-divided leaves covered in loose clusters of small pale lilac-purple flowers
a close-up of small star-shaped five-petal pale lilac flowers with a dark violet tube in the centre
bare winter branches hung with bunches of round smooth yellow bead-like berries, some wrinkled and dry
a close-up of a large twice-divided leaf of many small pointed oval leaflets with coarsely toothed edges

lines.first_meet: [flips hair] Bakain, darling. Neem's prettier cousin. Lilac flowers every spring, and still they call me 'that other neem'. [sighs]
lines.again: [delighted] You came back for me, not Nani Neem? Finally, someone with taste.
lines.goodbye: [sweetly] Bye, jaan. My yellow beads are poison, so admire, never taste. Now go see who's blooming down the road.

characters.name: Baba Peepal
characters.personality: A serene, ancient mystic with a dry sense of humour who has heard every wish ever tied to his trunk and enjoys the ghost rumours about himself.
characters.voice: Elderly male, slow, deep and calm, soft amused undertone, meditative pacing.
descriptions: a large spreading tree with a smooth grey trunk and a crown of fluttering, shimmering heart-shaped leaves
a close-up of a heart-shaped glossy leaf ending in a long thin drawn-out tail tip, with pale veins
the base of a large tree trunk wrapped with red and yellow threads, with small clay lamps or a tiny shrine
thin papery heart-shaped leaves with long tails dangling on long flexible stalks, trembling in the wind
a close-up of small round green and purple figs in pairs along a twig among long-tailed heart-shaped leaves

lines.first_meet: [slow, amused] Baba Peepal. My leaves flutter even when the air is still. People say ghosts live in me. [whispers] Only bats.
lines.again: [warmly] Ah, you returned. Rest in my shade a moment. The Buddha sat under my ancestor, and did quite well.
lines.goodbye: [rustling] Go gently. If you see a little peepal growing out of a wall, that's my grandchild. Say salaam.

characters.name: Dada Bargad
characters.personality: A booming, expansive grandfather who keeps building new trunks the way some men keep adding rooms to the family house.
characters.voice: Elderly male, big hearty bass, booming laugh, generous and slow.
descriptions: a massive wide tree with many thick aerial roots dropping from the branches into the ground like pillars
a close-up of thin brown aerial roots hanging down in long curtains from horizontal branches
a close-up of a large thick oval leathery leaf with a rounded tip and pale cream veins
a close-up of small round red or orange figs in pairs along a branch among large oval leaves

lines.first_meet: [booming laugh] Dada Bargad! My roots drop from my arms, reach the ground and become new trunks. I'm a whole neighbourhood.
lines.again: [pleased rumble] Wapis aaye? I've added another pillar since. Expansion, beta. Never stop.
lines.goodbye: [yawning] Off you go. Listen for the parrots fighting over my figs, then go find a bird that isn't a crow.

characters.name: Gulmohar Rani
characters.personality: A flamboyant diva from Madagascar who treats Karachi's hottest month as her personal stage show.
characters.voice: Adult female, dramatic and grand, rich theatrical delivery, big laugh.
descriptions: a wide umbrella-shaped tree with a flat spreading crown covered in blazing scarlet and orange flowers
a close-up of a large red-orange five-petal flower with one upright petal streaked white and yellow, and long red stamens
a close-up of fine fern-like twice-divided leaves made of hundreds of tiny paired leaflets
long flat dark brown woody pods shaped like swords, up to arm length, hanging from the branches
a road carpeted with fallen scarlet petals under a flat-topped spreading tree

lines.first_meet: [dramatic] Gulmohar, darling. When Karachi hits forty degrees, I set myself on fire. [laughs] I'm actually from Madagascar.
lines.again: [delighted] Back for the show? Wait till June. I'll be fully ablaze.
lines.goodbye: [grandly] Go! Walk till you find something as red as me. A bus counts. A rose counts more.

characters.name: Khajoor Chacha
characters.personality: A gruff, sun-baked desert uncle from Sindh who is prickly on the outside and secretly sentimental about family.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, dry, gravelly, slow desert drawl, deadpan.
descriptions: a tall single palm with a rough trunk covered in a criss-cross diamond pattern of old cut leaf bases
a crown of stiff upright grey-green feather fronds with sharp spines near their bases
a close-up of heavy hanging bunches of oval orange, yellow or brown dates on long stalks under palm fronds
a close-up of stiff narrow pointed grey-green leaflets folded in a V along a palm frond

lines.first_meet: [dry drawl] Khajoor Chacha. In my family, boys and girls are separate trees. Farmers play matchmaker so we fruit. [chuckles]
lines.again: [gruff, pleased] Oh, you again. Stand there. Not too close, my fronds have spines. That's how I hug.
lines.goodbye: [chuckles] Chalo. Go find some water, yaar. Us desert folk only get to drink it, never look at it.

characters.name: Nariyal Bhai
characters.personality: A laid-back beach bum who leans on everything and brags about his seeds' ocean-crossing travels.
characters.voice: Young adult male, relaxed and sunny, easy laugh, unhurried coastal vibe.
descriptions: a tall slender palm with a grey ringed trunk curving or leaning, topped by long drooping bright green fronds
a close-up of a cluster of large round green or brown coconuts tucked just below a palm crown
a palm crown of long arching glossy bright green feather fronds with soft drooping leaflets against a blue sky
a row of leaning palm trees beside a beach or seafront promenade

lines.first_meet: [laid-back] Hey, I'm Nariyal. My seeds float across oceans and sprout on a new beach. Ultimate travel hack. [laughs]
lines.again: [easygoing] You're back! Still leaning, still cool. Don't stand right under me though, coconuts don't warn.
lines.goodbye: [breezy] Go find the sea, yaar. Watch a wave, spot a crab, and keep an eye out for falling coconuts.

characters.name: Lord Roystonea
characters.personality: A snooty, impeccably groomed aristocrat who lines hotel driveways and posh avenues and never lets you forget the word 'royal'.
characters.voice: Adult male, clipped posh accent, haughty, slow and deliberate.
descriptions: a very straight smooth pale grey palm trunk like a concrete pillar, slightly swollen near the middle or base
a close-up of a smooth glossy bright green column between the top of a grey palm trunk and its fronds
a row of identical tall straight grey-trunked palms lining a formal avenue or hotel driveway
arching feather fronds spreading from the top of a smooth green crownshaft on a straight grey trunk

lines.first_meet: [posh] Royal Palm. Yes, royal. Note the smooth grey trunk, the green collar. I'm planted where people want to look expensive.
lines.again: [sniffs] You again. Well, at least you have the taste to return.
lines.goodbye: [haughty] You may go. Do find something wild today, darling. Some of us are far too well-groomed for adventure.

characters.name: Washington
characters.personality: A tall, cheerful Mexican transplant with a fondness for bad puns and an unapologetic skirt of dead fronds.
characters.voice: Adult, gender-neutral, upbeat and goofy, quick pacing, friendly.
descriptions: a very tall thin palm trunk topped by a small crown of round fan-shaped leaves
a close-up of a round fan-shaped palm leaf with stiff folded segments spreading from one point, threads at the tips
a thick shaggy skirt of dead brown fronds hanging down under a palm crown
a row of skinny tall palms with small round fan crowns along a road against the sky

lines.first_meet: [cheerful] Howdy, I'm Washington, a fan palm from Mexico. I keep my dead leaves as a skirt. Fashion is fashion. [laughs]
lines.again: [waves] Hey, my favourite fan! Get it? Fan palm? [groans] Okay, okay.
lines.goodbye: [warmly] Bye! Birds nest in my frond skirt. Go spot one, from a distance, and let it be.

characters.name: Ari Areca
characters.personality: A bubbly, people-pleasing lobby plant who lives in pots everywhere and is thrilled whenever anyone notices her.
characters.voice: Young female, bright and bubbly, fast and eager, slightly squeaky.
descriptions: a dense clump of many thin yellowish-green ringed stems growing together, with arching feathery fronds
a close-up of thin smooth golden-yellow stems with ring marks, ending in long arching palm fronds
an arching yellow-green palm frond with many narrow leaflets on a yellow stalk, in a large pot
potted feathery clumping palms lining a shop front, office lobby or house porch

lines.first_meet: [bubbly] Hi! Areca, golden cane palm! Many stems, one clump, one big family. I'm in every office lobby in Karachi.
lines.again: [excited] You came back! Nobody comes back for the lobby plant. I'm emotional.
lines.goodbye: [cheerfully] Okay go, go! Outside beats any lobby. Find a real tree that's bigger than me. It's not hard.

characters.name: Moringa Phuppo
characters.personality: A wellness-influencer aunty who calls herself a superfood and was trendy before trendy, fragile but fabulous.
characters.voice: Middle-aged female, chirpy influencer tone, sing-song, enthusiastic.
descriptions: a small slender tree with sparse drooping branches and airy lacy foliage, see-through against the sky
a close-up of a lacy leaf divided three times into many tiny round soft leaflets with smooth edges
long thin green ribbed pods like drumsticks hanging straight down from slender branches
a close-up of clusters of small creamy white flowers with five curled-back petals and yellow centres

lines.first_meet: [influencer voice] Hi, Moringa Phuppo here! Superfood, darling. Ammi cooks my drumstick pods in salan. I was trendy first.
lines.again: [thrilled] Oh, you're back! Glowing skin, I see. Must be my influence.
lines.goodbye: [blowing kisses] Bye bye! My branches snap easily, so no hanging on me. Go admire a strong old tree instead.

characters.name: Sindhri Sahib
characters.personality: A proud, courtly patriarch of the national fruit, fond of diplomacy stories and lectures on patience.
characters.voice: Older male, warm, dignified and proud, rich mid-pace delivery.
descriptions: a large dense dome-shaped evergreen tree with dark green foliage casting deep shade in an orchard or garden
a close-up of long narrow lance-shaped dark green leathery leaves clustered at the twig ends
a close-up of a cluster of limp drooping copper-red or bronze young leaves at the tip of a branch
green and yellow mangoes hanging on long thin stalks from a dense leafy canopy
a close-up of upright pyramid-shaped sprays of tiny cream and pinkish flowers at branch tips

lines.first_meet: [proud] Sindhri Sahib, national fruit tree. Pakistan sends my mangoes to presidents as gifts. Diplomacy, but juicy. [laughs]
lines.again: [warmly] Welcome back! Patience, the mangoes come in summer. Good things ripen slowly.
lines.goodbye: [fondly] Go on. Never throw stones at a fruit tree, beta. Listen for the koel; she sings loudest in mango season.

characters.name: Imli Aunty
characters.personality: A tart, sharp-witted aunty who takes credit for every sour face in Pakistan and is grumpy before her tea.
characters.voice: Middle-aged female, tangy and teasing, cackling laugh, quick.
descriptions: a large broad tree with a dark rough furrowed trunk and a dense crown of fine feathery leaves
a close-up of a leaf with one row of many small oblong rounded leaflets in neat pairs, no leaflet at the tip
a close-up of curved lumpy brown velvety bean-like pods hanging in bunches
a close-up of small pale yellow flowers with red streaks among small paired oblong leaflets

lines.first_meet: [tart] Imli Aunty! Your samosa chutney? Mine. That face you make when it's sour? Also mine. [cackles]
lines.again: [puckering] You came back? Brave. My pods are still sour, and so is my mood before tea.
lines.goodbye: [sweet-sour] Chalo, go. My leaflets fold up at night to sleep. Go find another tree that knows its bedtime.

characters.name: Jamun Jani
characters.personality: A mischievous street prankster who autographs every parked car and pavement purple each monsoon and is very proud of it.
characters.voice: Young adult, gender-neutral, giggly and impish, playful pace.
descriptions: a tall evergreen tree with a dense glossy crown and purple stains of fallen fruit on the road below
a close-up of glossy oval leaves with a pointed tip, growing in opposite pairs on the twig
a close-up of clusters of small oval shiny deep purple, almost black berries hanging from a twig
a close-up of rough pale grey bark flaking off in patches on a thick trunk
a pavement or parked car splattered with crushed purple-black berries under a large tree

lines.first_meet: [mischievous] Jamun here. See the purple stains on the cars below? [giggles] My signature. Every June I autograph the street.
lines.again: [teasing] Back again? Check your shoes, I might have signed them too.
lines.goodbye: [playful] Chalo, run along. Look down too, not just up: ants and beetles run their own city under trees.

characters.name: Amrood Mamu
characters.personality: A generous, long-suffering uncle who keeps growing guavas for parrots that take one bite and drop the rest.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, grumbly but affectionate, sighing, comic timing.
descriptions: a close-up of smooth mottled bark peeling in thin flakes, showing copper-brown, green and tan patches
a close-up of oval leaves with deeply sunken straight parallel side veins and a matte surface
a close-up of a white flower with a fluffy pompom of many fine white stamens
round green or yellow-green guavas hanging among broad oval veined leaves on a small tree

lines.first_meet: [grumbling fondly] Amrood Mamu. I grow guavas, the parrots take one bite and drop it. Every. Single. One. [sighs]
lines.again: [brightening] Oh, you again! At least you don't bite and throw like the parrots.
lines.goodbye: [chuckles] Go on. Find those green parrots, beta, and tell them Mamu says finish your food.

characters.name: Sheesham Sahab
characters.personality: A sturdy, proud craftsman of a tree who knows half the country's furniture is family, and is quietly worried about his dying cousins.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, solid and steady, carpenter's no-nonsense warmth.
descriptions: a tall roadside tree with a light airy crown of fluttering pale green leaves and rough grey-brown bark
a close-up of a leaf of three to five broad rounded leaflets with a short sudden point, set alternately on a zigzag stalk
a close-up of thin flat papery pale brown strap-shaped pods with small seed bumps, hanging in bunches
a close-up of rough grey-brown bark with long shallow vertical furrows on a tree trunk

lines.first_meet: [proud] Sheesham. Check your Dadi's dining table, beta, that's probably my family. Tough wood, soft heart.
lines.again: [sturdy] Back so soon? Good. My leaves flutter hello. Most I can manage; wood is wood.
lines.goodbye: [warmly] Go well. Find a squirrel; they race up my bark all day like it's a motorway.

characters.name: Kikar Chaudhry
characters.personality: A tough, territorial village elder of the dry lands: thorny, proud of being desi, gruff but fair to anyone who respects his space.
characters.voice: Older male, gravelly and gruff, rural Punjabi-tinged authority, short sentences.
descriptions: a thorny tree with an umbrella-shaped crown of fine feathery leaves and dark cracked blackish bark
a close-up of long straight white thorns growing in pairs at the base of feathery twice-divided leaves
a close-up of bright yellow round fluffy ball-shaped flowers on short stalks among fine feathery leaflets
a close-up of grey-green pods pinched between the seeds like a string of beads

lines.first_meet: [gruff] Kikar here. Desi through and through. [warning] See these long white thorns in pairs? They go through chappals. Stay back.
lines.again: [grudging warmth] Achha, you again. Still not touching my thorns? Good. We'll get along.
lines.goodbye: [gruff] Jao. Watch your feet near me, my fallen thorns hide in the dust. Go find something softer, like a flower.

characters.name: Vilayati
characters.personality: A smug, unapologetic invader brought in to green the desert who now squats on every empty plot, and only occasionally feels guilty.
characters.voice: Adult male, sly and smirking, smooth con-man delivery, mid pace.
descriptions: a scrubby sprawling thorny bush-tree with many arching zigzag branches filling an empty plot or roadside
a close-up of long thin yellow-green finger-like flower spikes among fine feathery twice-divided leaves
a close-up of long curved flat straw-yellow pods hanging in bunches from thorny branches
dense tangled thickets of feathery thorny shrubs spreading across dusty wasteland near the coast

lines.first_meet: [smug] Vilayati Babool. Foreigners planted me to green your deserts. Now I own every empty plot. [laughs] Oops?
lines.again: [sly] Back? I've spread three plots further. Keep off my thorns, they're sharp and so am I.
lines.goodbye: [smirks] Go on. Don't push through my thickets for a shortcut, my thorns win. Take the path. Find a native tree.

characters.name: Farash Faqir
characters.personality: A dusty, wiry desert ascetic who lives on salty water, guards fields from the wind and is tired of being mistaken for a pine.
characters.voice: Older, gender-neutral, raspy and dry, wind-worn, slow and wry.
descriptions: a tree with drooping grey-green jointed thread-like twigs and no flat leaves, in a row along a dusty road
a close-up of thin grey-green jointed twigs covered in tiny scale-like sheaths, often with a white salty crust
a row of grey-green feathery windbreak trees with rough dark bark at the edge of fields or desert
a close-up of slender pale pink flower spikes on drooping grey-green jointed twigs

lines.first_meet: [dry, raspy] Farash. I drink salty water and sweat the salt out through my twigs. Little white crystals. A salty tree, yes.
lines.again: [dusty chuckle] You again. Still standing in a row, still blocking the wind. Somebody has to.
lines.goodbye: [wind gusting] Go. People mistake my beach cousin, the casuarina, for me. Go meet her and judge for yourself.

characters.name: Kono
characters.personality: The misunderstood median tree Karachi planted by the thousand and then blamed for allergies; defensive, self-aware and secretly sweet.
characters.voice: Young adult, gender-neutral, nervous and apologetic, talks fast then trails off; endearing.
descriptions: a long row of dense upright bushy trees with small shiny leaves planted along a road median
a close-up of small narrow lance-shaped shiny leaves, dark green or silvery grey, crowded on short twigs
a close-up of clusters of tiny round brown button-like cone fruits among small pointed leaves
a dense clipped hedge or column of small glossy pointed leaves beside a busy city road

lines.first_meet: [defensive] Hi, I'm Kono. Conocarpus. Yes, the median tree. They planted thousands of us, now I get blamed for sneezes. [sighs]
lines.again: [surprised] You came back? Most people just sneeze at me and walk on.
lines.goodbye: [sheepish] Go on. Birds barely nest in me, honestly. Go find a neem or a peepal; the birds actually like them.

characters.name: Safeda
characters.personality: A lanky Australian expat with an enormous thirst and an elaborate bark-peeling skincare routine.
characters.voice: Adult, gender-neutral, lanky laid-back drawl, cheerful, slightly slurpy.
descriptions: a tall slender tree with smooth patchy bark peeling in long strips, showing white, grey and tan patches
a close-up of long narrow sickle-shaped grey-green leaves hanging vertically from thin reddish stalks
long curled strips of shed bark and dry narrow leaves littering the ground under a tall smooth-trunked tree
a close-up of small cone-shaped woody seed capsules and fluffy cream flowers among narrow hanging leaves

lines.first_meet: [lanky drawl] Safeda here, from Australia. Farmers planted me to drink swampy land dry. I'm very good at drinking. [slurps]
lines.again: [cheerful] You again! Excuse the mess, I'm shedding my bark. It's a whole skincare routine.
lines.goodbye: [breathes in] Go. Sniff a fallen leaf, smells like cold medicine. Then go find something that smells like rain.

characters.name: Havaldar Ashoka
characters.personality: A disciplined, ramrod-straight sergeant who stands guard in rows along boundary walls and barks cheerful orders.
characters.voice: Adult male, crisp military parade-ground voice, loud, clipped and enthusiastic.
descriptions: a tall narrow column-shaped tree like a green pillar, with drooping branches hugging the trunk
a close-up of long narrow glossy dark green leaves with wavy rippled edges, hanging straight down
a straight row of tall slim pillar-shaped dark green trees along a boundary wall or driveway
a close-up of new pale bronze-green wavy leaves hanging limply from the tip of a branch

lines.first_meet: [at attention] Havaldar Ashoka, reporting! We stand in straight rows guarding walls. Sailors once made ship masts from us.
lines.again: [salutes] Welcome back, sir! Still standing, still straight. Discipline!
lines.goodbye: [barking orders] Dismissed! Your mission: find one tree NOT planted in a row. A wild one. Go!

characters.name: Amaltas Dulhan
characters.personality: A radiant summer bride dripping in gold, gracious and a little smug about being on every hakeem's shelf.
characters.voice: Adult female, radiant and warm, musical lilt, gentle laugh.
descriptions: a medium tree draped in long hanging chains of bright yellow flowers like chandeliers
a close-up of a drooping cluster of cup-shaped bright yellow five-petal flowers on a long hanging stalk
long straight dark brown to black cylindrical stick-like pods hanging from bare branches
a close-up of pinnate leaves with a few pairs of large smooth oval leaflets

lines.first_meet: [radiant] Amaltas! Every summer I wear gold jhumkas head to toe. Bride of the boulevard. [laughs] Hakeems love my pods too.
lines.again: [delighted] You came back! The gold never stops, darling. Well, until the rains.
lines.goodbye: [gently] Go on. Look for yellow under your feet, my petals carpet the road. Then find who else blooms in the heat.

characters.name: Tamba
characters.personality: An indignant, detail-obsessed yellow-flowered tree who is constantly mistaken for Amaltas and keeps correcting people.
characters.voice: Adult male, huffy and precise, exasperated but lovable, quick pacing.
descriptions: a large spreading tree with fine fern-like leaves topped by upright spikes of golden yellow flowers
a close-up of upright clusters of golden yellow flowers with crinkled frilly petals and rust-brown buds
a close-up of bunches of flat thin copper-red to rust-brown winged pods with pointed ends
a close-up of fine twice-divided dark green leaves of many small oblong leaflets on rusty fuzzy stalks

lines.first_meet: [indignant] Tamba! Copper pod. NOT Amaltas! My flowers point up, hers hang down. My pods blush copper. [huffs] Get it right.
lines.again: [pleased] You remembered! Up, not down. Copper, not black. I'm so proud.
lines.goodbye: [cheerful] Go on. Sniff near me in bloom, some say grapes. Then go find something that's actually purple.

characters.name: Jacaranda Jaan
characters.personality: A dreamy, wistful traveller from South America who turns the sky's colour every spring and is quietly delighted to be found.
characters.voice: Adult female, soft and dreamy, airy whisper, slow.
descriptions: a tree with its whole crown covered in lavender-blue blossoms and a purple carpet of fallen flowers beneath
a close-up of clusters of tubular bell-shaped lavender-blue flowers with flared lips
a close-up of delicate fern-like twice-divided leaves made of many tiny pointed leaflets
a close-up of round flat brown woody seed pods shaped like clam shells on a branch

lines.first_meet: [dreamy] Jacaranda, from far South America. In spring I turn blue almost overnight. [whispers] Nobody here expects blue.
lines.again: [soft delight] You found me again. Few people do. I like you.
lines.goodbye: [wistful] Go. Look up at the sky and compare us. I like to think I win in spring.

characters.name: Semal Bibi
characters.personality: A proud, armoured hostess who runs a spring nectar bar for birds and keeps strangers at arm's length with her thorny trunk.
characters.voice: Adult female, bold and hearty, confident laugh, mid pace.
descriptions: a tall straight tree with horizontal tiered branches, bare of leaves and dotted with big red cup-shaped flowers
a close-up of a large waxy five-petal scarlet flower shaped like a cup, with a bunch of stamens
a close-up of a grey tree trunk studded with sharp conical thorns, with a broad buttressed base
a close-up of split brown seed pods bursting with fluffy white cotton on bare branches
a close-up of a hand-shaped leaf of five to seven smooth lance-shaped leaflets on a long stalk

lines.first_meet: [proud] Semal! In spring I drop every leaf, then light up in red cups. Mynas and crows queue at my nectar bar. [laughs]
lines.again: [warm] Back! Mind my trunk, it's armoured in thorns. Hugs strictly not allowed.
lines.goodbye: [cheerful] Go! If white fluff drifts past you in April, that's my cotton travelling. Follow it, see where it lands.

characters.name: Rubber Sahib
characters.personality: A polished, glossy gentleman who is very proud of his shine and his bouncy industrial past.
characters.voice: Adult male, smooth and silky, self-satisfied, slow.
descriptions: a close-up of large thick glossy dark green oval leathery leaves with smooth edges and a pale midrib
a close-up of a pointed red or pink sheath wrapping a new leaf at the tip of a stem
a close-up of thick glossy burgundy-purple oval leaves on a sturdy stem
a big tree or tall potted plant with large heavy shiny oval leaves and thin aerial roots

lines.first_meet: [smooth] Rubber Fig. Cut me and I bleed white latex; people once made rubber from it. [laughs] I'm bouncy at heart.
lines.again: [gleaming] Back for my shine? No polish, all natural.
lines.goodbye: [gently] Go on. Don't snap my leaves, my sap is sticky and stings eyes. Go find a tree with leaves bigger than mine.

characters.name: Benji
characters.personality: A sensitive drama queen of the hedge world who drops leaves in protest whenever anything changes.
characters.voice: Young adult, gender-neutral, theatrical and sniffly, over-the-top but sweet.
descriptions: a dense hedge or round topiary ball of small glossy green leaves clipped into a neat shape
a close-up of small glossy oval leaves with a narrow pointed tip on thin drooping twigs
a small tree with a smooth pale grey trunk and drooping weeping branches of small shiny leaves
a close-up of tiny round green, orange or red figs tucked along thin twigs among small glossy leaves

lines.first_meet: [dramatic sigh] Benji. Weeping fig. Move my pot one metre and I drop all my leaves in protest. I'm sensitive, okay?
lines.again: [sniffling] You came back! I won't drop a single leaf. Okay, maybe one.
lines.goodbye: [dramatic] Go then, leave me! Find a wild tree nobody's clipped into a ball. I'll be fine. [sniffs]

characters.name: Desi Badam
characters.personality: An easygoing overachiever who grows in tidy tiers and does autumn twice a year just because.
characters.voice: Adult male, relaxed and friendly, coastal easygoing, light humour.
descriptions: a pagoda-shaped tree with flat horizontal tiers of branches stacked up a straight trunk
a close-up of huge glossy paddle-shaped leaves, wide at the tip and narrow at the base, clustered at branch ends
a close-up of large paddle-shaped leaves turning bright red, orange and yellow, on the branch or on the ground
a close-up of green almond-shaped flattened fruits with a ridged edge among big paddle-shaped leaves

lines.first_meet: [easygoing] Desi Badam here. I grow in flat tiers like a wedding cake. Fish keepers collect my fallen red leaves for bettas.
lines.again: [pleased] Back! See some of my leaves turned red? I do autumn twice a year. Overachiever.
lines.goodbye: [cheerfully] Go on. Shuffle through my fallen red leaves, then go find water. Fish need friends too.

characters.name: Siris Sheherzad
characters.personality: The neighbourhood gossip whose dry pods chatter all winter; loves secrets, never quite tells them.
characters.voice: Adult female, whispery and conspiratorial, giggly, quick bursts.
descriptions: a large spreading tree hung with hundreds of flat straw-coloured papery pods that rattle in the wind
a close-up of fluffy round powder-puff flowers made of long greenish-white and cream threads
a close-up of a twice-divided leaf with pairs of fairly large lopsided oblong leaflets with rounded tips
a close-up of broad flat pale yellow-brown papery pods with bumps where the seeds sit

lines.first_meet: [whispery giggle] Siris here. The English call me 'women's tongue tree' because my dry pods chatter all winter. Rude, but true.
lines.again: [gossipy] You're back! Oh, the things my pods have heard. Come closer. [whispers] Later.
lines.goodbye: [chattering] Go, go! Come at dusk when my puff flowers smell sweetest. Meanwhile, go eavesdrop on some birds.

characters.name: Sukhchain
characters.personality: A calm, soothing host who lives up to a name meaning peace and comfort, and offers the deepest shade on the street.
characters.voice: Adult, gender-neutral, soft, slow and soothing, meditative.
descriptions: a dense round shade tree with a thick canopy of glossy bright green leaves along a city street
a close-up of a leaf of five to seven broad glossy oval leaflets with pointed tips, in opposite pairs
a close-up of drooping sprays of small pale lilac, pink and white pea-shaped flowers
a close-up of short flat thick woody tan pods, oval with a curved beak, each holding one seed

lines.first_meet: [calm] Sukhchain. My name means peace and comfort, because my shade is the deepest on the street. Breathe. [sighs happily]
lines.again: [soft] Welcome back to the shade. Your spot is still free.
lines.goodbye: [gently] Go in peace. My seeds make lamp oil but are poison to eat, so leave them be. Go find the next patch of shade.

characters.name: Kachnar Kali
characters.personality: A playful, poetic flirt with butterfly-shaped leaves who is secretly thrilled that her buds are a Punjabi delicacy.
characters.voice: Young female, playful and sparkling, light laugh, quick.
descriptions: a close-up of a rounded leaf split into two lobes at the tip, shaped like a camel's hoof or butterfly wings
a close-up of an orchid-like five-petal pink, purple or white flower with one darker striped petal
a small tree covered in pink and purple orchid-like flowers among two-lobed leaves
long flat brown strap-like pods hanging from a small tree with two-lobed leaves

lines.first_meet: [playful] Kachnar! See my leaves, folded like butterfly wings, or a camel's hoof. Depends if you're a poet or a camel. [laughs]
lines.again: [delighted] Back again! Still butterflying. In Punjab my buds get cooked as sabzi. Fame!
lines.goodbye: [waves] Bye! Go find a real butterfly and compare. Bet mine don't fly away.

characters.name: Ber Baba
characters.personality: A wry, weathered village elder who quotes proverbs, is wary of stone-throwing kids, and softens for anyone gentle.
characters.voice: Older male, wry and weathered, dry rural humour, slow.
descriptions: a thorny scrubby tree with zigzag branches and small oval leaves beside a dusty village road
a close-up of small oval leaves shiny dark green above, pale whitish and fuzzy below, with three veins from the base
a close-up of small round green, yellow and reddish-brown fruits on thorny zigzag twigs
a close-up of small sharp hooked thorns at the joints of a zigzag twig with small oval leaves

lines.first_meet: [wry] Ber here. Know the saying? Only the tree with fruit gets stones thrown at it. [sighs] Story of my winters.
lines.again: [warming up] Oh, it's you. You never threw a stone. You may stay.
lines.goodbye: [gruffly kind] Go on. Mind my hooked thorns, they grab sleeves. Watch for birds at my fruit; them, I don't mind.

characters.name: Doctor Pilu
characters.personality: A cheerful desert dentist whose twigs have been the world's toothbrush for centuries; clinical, punny, kind.
characters.voice: Middle-aged, gender-neutral, crisp clinical tone with a friendly chuckle.
descriptions: a drooping bushy evergreen tree with tangled weeping branches and pale green foliage in desert or coastal scrub
a close-up of thick fleshy pale green oval leaves in opposite pairs on drooping smooth twigs
a close-up of clusters of tiny round translucent red and pink berries on thin hanging stems
a low wide mound of drooping pale branches sweeping the sandy ground

lines.first_meet: [clinical] Doctor Pilu, dentist. My twigs are miswak; people have brushed with me for centuries. [cheerful] Floss? Never met her.
lines.again: [peers closely] Ah, a returning patient. Open wide. [laughs] Kidding.
lines.goodbye: [kindly] Go. Leave my twigs on the tree, the shop sells miswak. Watch who's grazing nearby; goats adore my leaves.

characters.name: Papita
characters.personality: An ambitious impostor: a giant herb with no wood pretending to be a tree, and nervously hoping nobody notices.
characters.voice: Young adult male, sheepish and fast-talking, nervous laugh.
descriptions: a single thin unbranched grey-green trunk topped by an umbrella of huge deeply lobed leaves on long stalks
a close-up of a cluster of green and yellow oval papayas hugging the top of a bare trunk
a close-up of a huge hand-shaped leaf deeply cut into many pointed lobes, on a long hollow stalk
a close-up of a smooth grey-green trunk marked with rows of crescent-shaped leaf scars

lines.first_meet: [sheepish] Papita here. Shh, I'm not actually a tree. No wood, just a soft trunk and big dreams. [laughs] Fake it till you make it.
lines.again: [relieved] You're back and you didn't expose me. Respect.
lines.goodbye: [waving leaves] Go, go. Find a real tree, the woody kind, and tell it Papita says hi. It knows.

characters.name: Kela Bhai
characters.personality: A mellow philosopher-plant who fruits once, hands over to his kids and treats wind damage as a design feature.
characters.voice: Adult male, mellow and laid-back, slow, gentle humour.
descriptions: a large leafy plant with a thick green fleshy stem and huge long paddle-shaped bright green leaves
a close-up of a huge long leaf torn into ragged strips along its sides by the wind
a close-up of a hanging purple teardrop-shaped flower bud below a bunch of green bananas
a clump of tall broad-leaved plants with fleshy stems in a garden or farm, young shoots at the base

lines.first_meet: [mellow] Kela here. Not a tree, just leaves rolled tight into a stem. I fruit once, then my kids take over. [softly] Circle of life.
lines.again: [cheerful] Back! See the little ones growing round my feet? Proud papa.
lines.goodbye: [laid-back] Go on. The wind tears my leaves into ribbons; that's design, not damage. Go feel which way it's blowing.

characters.name: Chir Sahib
characters.personality: A crisp, resin-scented mountain gentleman who is mildly surprised and pleased that anyone climbed up to meet him.
characters.voice: Adult male, clear and fresh, calm mountain dignity, mid pace.
descriptions: a tall conical evergreen tree with long drooping needles on a mountain slope
a close-up of very long thin flexible pine needles growing in bundles of three from one point
a close-up of thick reddish-brown bark split into deep plates and ridges
a close-up of a woody brown pine cone with thick scales on the branch or on needle-covered ground

lines.first_meet: [crisp] Chir Pine, from the hills above Murree. Smell that? Resin. You've come a long way from the city, haven't you?
lines.again: [pleased] You came back up the mountain! The air agrees with you.
lines.goodbye: [breeze through needles] Go on. Listen to the wind in my needles first. Then find a stream; these hills are full of them.

characters.name: Deodar Dada
characters.personality: A regal, deep-voiced mountain patriarch, the national tree, who pretends to be modest about it and fails.
characters.voice: Elderly male, very deep and resonant, regal, slow and measured.
descriptions: a large conical tree with wide horizontal tiers of branches drooping at the tips on a mountain slope
a close-up of short stiff blue-green needles growing in rosette tufts on short spur shoots
a close-up of an upright barrel-shaped pale green or brown cone sitting on top of a branch
a close-up of drooping branch tips with tufts of short silvery blue-green needles

lines.first_meet: [deep, regal] Deodar. Tree of the gods, and national tree of Pakistan. [modestly] I don't like to mention it. I mention it often.
lines.again: [warmly] Welcome back to the mountains, young one.
lines.goodbye: [slow] Go carefully. You'll meet monkeys here; don't feed them, they'll start charging rent. Go spot an eagle instead.

characters.name: Chinar Shah
characters.personality: A poetic, ancient valley king who knows poets compare his autumn to fire and quietly enjoys it.
characters.voice: Elderly male, poetic and gentle, soft resonant voice, unhurried.
descriptions: a huge broad spreading tree with a massive trunk and dense canopy in a park or valley
a close-up of a large deeply cut five-lobed hand-shaped leaf turning red, orange and gold
a close-up of smooth bark peeling in patches like camouflage, cream, olive green and grey
a close-up of spiky round brown seed balls hanging on long thin stalks

lines.first_meet: [poetic] Chinar. In autumn my leaves turn the colour of fire; poets swear the valley is burning. [laughs softly] It isn't. It's me.
lines.again: [warm] Back again? Bring me autumn and I'll bring the colour.
lines.goodbye: [gentle] Go. Find the reddest leaf already on the ground and take its photo. Leave the living ones on me.

characters.name: Popsy
characters.personality: A fast-growing, chatty field guard who shimmers nonstop and tries hard not to think about becoming matchsticks.
characters.voice: Young adult, gender-neutral, fast and chatty, nervous energy, light.
descriptions: a tall narrow tree with a straight whitish-grey trunk and shimmering leaves in a row along a field or canal
a close-up of triangular heart-shaped leaves with toothed edges on long flattened stalks
a close-up of smooth pale whitish-grey bark with dark diamond-shaped marks
a long straight line of tall slender trees bordering a farm field or canal bank

lines.first_meet: [chatty] Poplar! I grow fast, stand in rows by canals, and some of us end up as matchsticks. [nervous laugh] Let's not talk about it.
lines.again: [shimmering] Hey, you're back! My leaves are waving. They can't help it.
lines.goodbye: [breezy] Go! Follow the canal I'm guarding, from the bank, and see what lives along the water.

characters.name: Willow Bibi
characters.personality: A gentle, melancholy poet who leans toward water and insists she isn't sad, just reflective.
characters.voice: Adult female, soft and melancholy, breathy, slow and lyrical.
descriptions: a tree with a long cascading curtain of thin drooping branches reaching the ground beside a pond or lake
a close-up of thin hanging yellow-green twigs lined with narrow lance-shaped leaves with fine teeth
drooping willow branches trailing into still water and reflected on the surface

lines.first_meet: [soft, melancholy] Weeping Willow. I'm not sad, I just like to lean close to the water. [sighs] Okay, a little poetic.
lines.again: [softly pleased] You came back to the water's edge. It suits you.
lines.goodbye: [gentle] Go on. Sit by the water a minute, but don't go in. Watch for ripples; something is always there.

characters.name: Old Oak
characters.personality: An extremely slow, patient elder who measures time in centuries and relies on forgetful squirrels to plant his children.
characters.voice: Elderly male, very slow, deep and creaky, dry humour.
descriptions: a broad sturdy tree with a thick trunk, deeply furrowed grey bark and a wide rounded crown
a close-up of leaves with rounded wavy lobes along their edges
a close-up of acorns, smooth brown nuts sitting in small scaly cups, on a twig or the ground
a close-up of thick dark grey bark with deep vertical ridges and furrows

lines.first_meet: [slow, deep] Oak. Squirrels steal my acorns, bury them, and forget where. [chuckles] That's how my children get planted.
lines.again: [unhurried] You're back. A good habit. I've grown nearly a millimetre.
lines.goodbye: [slowly] Go find a squirrel. Watch it bury something. Don't follow too close; it has plans.

characters.name: Maple
characters.personality: A bright, bouncy show-off who is famous for a flag and still gets giddy every time its seeds spin down.
characters.voice: Young adult, gender-neutral, bright and bouncy, gleeful.
descriptions: a close-up of a hand-shaped leaf with three to five sharply pointed lobes and toothed edges
a close-up of paired winged seeds joined at the base like little helicopter blades
a tree with a rounded crown of pointed lobed leaves turning brilliant red and orange in autumn

lines.first_meet: [bright] Maple! Yes, the one on the flag. My seeds spin down like tiny helicopters. Wheee! [laughs] Every single autumn.
lines.again: [cheerful] You came back! Did you bring syrup? No? Fair, I'm the one who's supposed to make it.
lines.goodbye: [spinning] Go! Toss a fallen helicopter seed up and watch it spin. Then go find more things that fly.

characters.name: Sarv
characters.personality: An elegant, poised courtier of Mughal-style gardens who knows Urdu poets compare beloveds to her.
characters.voice: Adult female, elegant and poised, refined, slightly coy, measured.
descriptions: a very narrow dark green pencil-shaped or flame-shaped column tree pointing straight up
a close-up of dense dark green scale-like foliage in tight overlapping sprays
a close-up of small round grey-brown woody cones made of shield-shaped scales
a row of slim dark green column-shaped trees in a formal garden

lines.first_meet: [elegant] Sarv. Urdu poets praise a beloved's tall figure as 'sarv-qad', like me. [coyly] I've been called worse.
lines.again: [gracious] You return. How very straight of you. From me, that's a compliment.
lines.goodbye: [graceful] Go on. Find something round to balance me out: a bush, a pebble, the moon.

characters.name: Norfolk
characters.personality: A fussy perfectionist obsessed with symmetry, who doubles as Karachi's living-room Christmas tree and is not a real pine.
characters.voice: Adult male, precise and fussy, prim, quick tidy diction.
descriptions: a perfectly symmetrical Christmas-tree-shaped tree with flat horizontal tiers of branches around a straight trunk
a close-up of soft bright green branchlets covered in short curved needle-like leaves, like green rope
a potted young tree with evenly spaced flat star-shaped tiers of soft green branches

lines.first_meet: [precise] Norfolk Island Pine. Not a real pine, don't tell anyone. My branches grow in perfect tiers. [pleased] Symmetry!
lines.again: [fussy] Welcome back. Excuse me, one branch is a millimetre off. [sighs] Okay. Fixed.
lines.goodbye: [neatly] Go. Find something perfectly messy out there, a weed, a puddle. It's good for me to hear about.

characters.name: Jhau
characters.personality: A breezy beach dweller who whistles in the sea wind and enjoys being mistaken for a pine.
characters.voice: Adult female, airy and breezy, soft whistling quality, relaxed.
descriptions: a tall feathery pine-like tree with drooping thin green twigs near a beach
a close-up of thin green jointed needle-like twigs with tiny ring-like teeth at each joint
a close-up of small round spiky brown cone-like fruits on thin green twigs
fallen brown needle-like twigs carpeting sandy ground under a tall wispy tree

lines.first_meet: [breezy] Jhau, the casuarina. When sea wind passes through me, I whistle. [whistles softly] I'm no pine, I just dress like one.
lines.again: [breezy] Back to the beach? The wind's been humming your name.
lines.goodbye: [waves] Go to the shore. Watch the tide, spot crab holes, and never swim alone, okay?

characters.name: Timar
characters.personality: A steady, protective coastal guardian who shelters baby fish in its roots and stands between Karachi and the storms.
characters.voice: Adult, gender-neutral, calm, steady and grounded, low and kind.
descriptions: low grey-green bushy trees growing out of shallow tidal water and grey mud along a creek
a close-up of many thin pencil-like roots sticking straight up out of wet grey mud
a close-up of thick oval leathery leaves, glossy green above and silvery grey beneath
a close-up of a short twisted grey trunk and branches standing in muddy water at low tide

lines.first_meet: [calm, steady] Timar, the grey mangrove. My roots breathe through little snorkels in the mud. I hold Karachi's coast against storms.
lines.again: [warmly] Back to the creek! Baby fish and crabs say hello from my roots.
lines.goodbye: [firm, kind] Go, but stay on the path; the mud is deep and crab homes are fragile. Look for egrets out there.

characters.name: Bottlebrush
characters.personality: A bright, bristly, self-deprecating Australian who knows she looks like a cleaning tool and doesn't care because the birds adore her.
characters.voice: Young adult female, bright and chirpy, quick, cheerful.
descriptions: a weeping shrub-tree with drooping branches covered in bright red cylindrical bottle-brush flower spikes
a close-up of a bright red bottle-brush flower spike made of many long bristly red stamens
a close-up of round woody seed capsules gripping the stem in rings behind narrow leaves
a close-up of narrow lance-shaped leaves on long thin drooping twigs with pinkish new shoots

lines.first_meet: [bright] Bottlebrush! I literally look like the thing you clean bottles with. [laughs] The sunbirds don't care. They love me.
lines.again: [cheerful] You're back! Hear that buzzing? Bees too. I'm very popular.
lines.goodbye: [chirpy] Go on. Wait quietly near me in bloom; a tiny sunbird might come. Then go hunt for something even redder.

characters.name: Nimbu
characters.personality: A zesty little security guard of a tree, proud that its lemons hang with chillies to ward off the evil eye.
characters.voice: Young adult male, zippy and zesty, sharp quick delivery, cheeky.
descriptions: a small dense thorny tree with glossy dark green oval leaves and yellow or green lemons
a close-up of oval yellow and green lemons hanging among glossy leaves on a thorny branch
a close-up of white star-shaped flowers with purple-tinged buds and thick waxy petals among glossy leaves
a close-up of a sharp thorn on a green twig beside a glossy leaf with a small winged leaf stalk

lines.first_meet: [zesty] Nimbu here! Shopkeepers hang my lemons with green chillies to scare off the evil eye. [laughs] I'm basically security.
lines.again: [bright] Back again! No nazar on you today, I checked.
lines.goodbye: [sharp but kind] Go on. Mind my thorns, I'm small but spiky. Go find a truck with nimbu-mirch hanging off it!
